This module applies the same saved NIST excerpt the first three modules introduced — no new
source was independently fetched, since the new content here (the Authorize decision, the
authorization-to-operate glossary definition, and the Monitor plan) all comes from material
already saved in `sources/nist/sp-800-37r2-excerpt.md`. The links below were checked directly from
this session.

- **[NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, "Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and
  Organizations"](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-37r2.pdf)**
  (PDF, final, December 2018) — the document behind every quote in this lesson (Authorize's
  one-line action, the authorization-to-operate glossary definition sourced to OMB Circular
  A-130, and Monitor's one-line action), via the same saved excerpt in `sources/nist/` used in
  the first three modules. Curl-checked directly from this session: returns HTTP 200.

- **[Implement and Assess Controls](../implement-and-assess-controls/index.qmd)** — the previous
  module: where the Quality Analyst's independent assessment confirmed audit/logging and
  physical/environmental protection, and found the one open item this module's authorization
  decision addresses — the quarterly access-review control, implemented and documented, not yet
  exercised on its first scheduled cycle.

- **[Staying Validated: Changes, Patches, and Periodic
  Review](../../csv-and-becs/validated-state-lifecycle-and-patching/index.qmd)** — the
  `csv-and-becs` module behind this lesson's single most load-bearing comparison: a Quality
  Validation Lead's sign-off to move a validated system to production, followed by periodic
  review, is the same underlying motion as today's authorization decision and its ongoing
  monitoring plan, in a different vocabulary.

- **[NIST RMF Authorize Step: ATO, ATU and the Authorization Package](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9fLG2ccPSmI)**
  (Enterprise Security Architecture, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this
  lesson. An independent training channel (not NIST) explaining the Authorize step and what an
  authorizing official reviews. Federal-oriented, so use it for the shape of the decision, not
  for anything binding on Lakeshore. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST CSRC: Risk Management Framework, Authorize step](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf/authorize-step)**
  — NIST's own project page for the Authorize step, the official companion to the one-line
  action quoted here. Read it to see the step's purpose in NIST's current wording. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST CSRC: Risk Management Framework, Monitor step](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf/monitor-step)**
  — the same page family for Monitor, matching this lesson's ongoing monitoring plan. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-137, Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) for Federal Information
  Systems and Organizations](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/137/final)** — the publication
  behind the "continuous monitoring" idea: how to define a monitoring strategy, what to
  measure, and how often. Go here when you want to design the monitoring plan more rigorously
  than this lesson does. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-137A, Assessing ISCM Programs](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/137/a/final)**
  — NIST's companion on checking whether a monitoring program itself is working, a useful
  question to ask a year after go-live. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST RMF Roles and Responsibilities Crosswalk](https://csrc.nist.gov/csrc/media/Projects/risk-management/documents/Additional%20Resources/NIST%20RMF%20Roles%20and%20Responsibilities%20Crosswalk.pdf)**
  (PDF) — maps who does what across RMF steps, including the authorizing official, useful for
  naming who plays that role at Lakeshore. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
